firstFive.what: A terminal trading screen for one Hyperliquid perpetuals account: a live candle chart on the left, and on the right the account's risk, the market's own numbers, a red-bordered proposal waiting for a click, the armed bot, and a running log.
firstFive.who: Someone trading this account with borrowed money, watching a program they armed, who has to decide on the agent's proposals without leaving the price.
firstFive.action: Read the pending block and click [ APPROVE ] or [ REFUSE ], or leave it and keep watching the position.

asked.requirement: A separate interface from the pro page, at its own route, leaving `/` untouched
asked.note: The page served at /trade with its own title PHOSPHOR TRADE. The pro page at / is untouched and keeps its own brief.

asked.requirement: Judged as a professional trading surface against what real perps desks carry, not against a
asked.note: Carries oracle, basis, funding at two periods, open interest, 24h volume and real volatility, none of which a retail app shows together.

asked.requirement: The same design language as the pro page: same tokens, same panel frame, same terminal
asked.note: Same box-drawing frame, same tokens from style.css, same monospace grid as the pro page. No new hue on the page except red on the liquidation surface.

asked.requirement: Everything on it readable and manipulable by the agent over MCP, not only by the human
asked.note: Overlay state comes from the server and the agent writes it. trade_focus, trade_highlight, trade_note, trade_overlay and trade_batch were all driven live and the payload read back.

asked.requirement: Components must not collide or conflict, at any width
asked.note: Measured every panel box against its neighbour at 390, 768 and 1440: no overlaps, no horizontal scroll, and no capped panel painting outside its box.

asked.requirement: Manual controls for cancel, close and flatten, reachable from the page
asked.note: CLOSE POSITION and CANCEL ALL on the position row, CANCEL on each order, FLATTEN ALL under the book, DISARM in the mandate row. All driven against live money.

asked.requirement: Positions and working orders drawn on the chart itself
asked.note: The position entry line is drawn on the chart, with the mandate stop-out and both stops pinned at the edge they went off, stacked so they do not overlap.

asked.requirement: Liquidation distance shown in ATR multiples as well as percent and dollars, because percent
asked.note: Reads 'LIQ at --, -- away, --, -- ATR'. All three units are present; they are dashes here because the venue returns no liquidation price on this cross position.

asked.requirement: Profit split into price, funding and fees, since a carry trade green on price can be red once
asked.note: The position row carries price and funding as separate figures beside the net number.

asked.requirement: Net and gross exposure with a plain sentence for a five percent adverse move, because cross
asked.note: Reads 'A 5% move against you leaves --', with net and gross on the line above it.

asked.requirement: Mark and oracle shown separately with the basis between them, as they are different prices
asked.note: Mark and oracle on their own lines with basis between them at +12.2 bps.

asked.requirement: The arm receipt: the account's next state if the program opens its maximum position
asked.note: Reads 'liquidation at $1,421.40, opens at most $60.00, free after $858.66, margin required $30.00'.

asked.requirement: Feed health beside the price, so a screen behind the market says so where price is read
asked.note: Reads 'feed LIVE ws 0s' in the status bar, next to the price rather than buried in the log.

asked.requirement: `null` renders as a dash and never as zero, because the venue reports an account value of 0.0
asked.note: Reads '--' over a hatched track, not 0 over an empty one. The hatch exists because an empty reverse meter claims you are at your liquidation.

asked.requirement: Every dynamic string reaches the DOM through textContent, never innerHTML
asked.note: grep for innerHTML in ui/trade.js returns nothing. Agent-authored text, log lines and venue errors all reach the DOM as text.

asked.requirement: Digits that tick must not change width
asked.note: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on every element carrying a number, so the fills column does not jitter as it updates.

asked.requirement: The kill switch reachable within two tab stops from a cold load, in every state
asked.note: Nothing focusable is written before it in the DOM, in any state. Verified in the flat, armed and kill-switch-on captures.

asked.requirement: No order ticket: where other interfaces put buy and sell, this puts the mandate console, and
asked.note: The mandate console occupies the place an order ticket would. There is no buy or sell control anywhere on the page.

asked.requirement: Working orders rendered as child rows of the position they belong to, not a table of their own
asked.note: Two stop orders render as indented, dimmer child rows directly under the ETH position they protect.

goal.outcome: A proposal that needs a human is decided where the human already is, and it is decided on the same facts the pro window would have shown.
goal.path: The red APPROVALS panel sits above MANDATE in the right column. It names what was proposed, its id and time, what the agent asked for, the policy lines going out and coming in, and why a click is needed. The two buttons sit under that text, in that order, nowhere else.
goal.why: On shot-1440.png the panel is the only red-bordered block on the screen and reads top to bottom: PENDING policy change, the id, the agent's sentence, the minus and plus lines, 'why: Policy changes always require a human click', then the buttons. Nothing above the buttons is decoration and nothing needed for the decision is off screen. Both windows render it from ui/approvals.js, so neither can show the shorter story.
